notes: Andante 24-hour pass 7 EUR (metro and bus); metro line E to the airport takes 30 minutes. Take CP trains to Douro, Guimarães and Aveiro (book online; right-hand window for the Douro). The hills are steep.
Summer is 25-30°C; São João night falls on 23 June (plastic hammers, fireworks), the Douro vineyards are green, and the Foz beaches are open (Atlantic 18°C).
Francesinha 12-15, pastel 1.30, port tasting 20-25, Lello 10 (counts towards a book), coffee 1; tip by rounding up.
Book Lello online for 09:00; do Clérigos in the morning; the Douro train is full on summer weekends, so book ahead; Bolhão market is closed.
Tripas à moda do Porto (tripe; locals are nicknamed 'tripeiros'), bacalhau, francesinha, vinho verde, tawny and ruby port.
Ribeira is safe at night; Gaia cellars close at 17:00.

transit.name: Andante 24-hour pass
transit.why_chosen: Metro, bus and tram; includes metro line E to the airport
transit.coverage: Metro do Porto, STCP otobüs, tramvay

stops.name: São Bento Station
stops.tips: A station hall lined with 20,000 azulejo tiles telling Portuguese history.

stops.name: Ribeira
stops.tips: UNESCO-listed riverside with colourful houses; take in Praça da Ribeira and the narrow lanes.

stops.name: Dom Luís I Bridge
stops.tips: A double-deck iron bridge by a student of Eiffel; walk across the upper level (next to the metro).

stops.name: Taylor's Port Cellars
stops.tips: A port cellar in Gaia dating from 1692; audio tour with 3 tastings and a garden terrace.

stops.name: Jardim do Morro
stops.tips: A garden at the bridge end; watch the Porto skyline at sunset, then take the cable car (6 EUR) down.

backups.name: Graham's Port Lodge
backups.tips: Vintage port and river views; an alternative to Taylor's.

backups.name: Mosteiro da Serra do Pilar
backups.tips: A terrace on the round monastery; on Gaia hill, with the best view.

stops.name: Livraria Lello
stops.tips: One of the world's most beautiful bookshops (red staircase); book an online ticket for the 09:00 opening (the price counts towards a book).

stops.name: Clérigos Tower
stops.tips: A 76 m Baroque tower with 240 steps; panoramic city views.

stops.name: Igreja do Carmo
stops.tips: Twin churches with a blue-tiled side facade; a 1 m wide house sits between them.

stops.name: Mercado do Bolhão
stops.tips: A restored 1914 market; try cheese and tinned sardines, and browse the upper-floor stalls.

stops.name: Café Majestic
stops.tips: A Belle Époque café from 1921; pricey but worth seeing, on Santa Catarina.

backups.name: Casa Guedes Praça Poveiros
backups.tips: Pernil (roast pork leg) sandwich with Serra cheese; expect a queue.

backups.name: Igreja de São Francisco
backups.tips: A gilded Baroque interior (300 kg of gold); also catacombs.

stops.name: Pinhão Station
stops.tips: The Linha do Douro train from São Bento takes 2.5 hours (along the river, sit by the right-hand window); the station is tiled.

stops.name: Quinta do Bomfim
stops.tips: Dow's vineyard; terrace tasting and a walk through the vines.

stops.name: Pinhão Rabelo Boat Tour
stops.tips: 1 hour on a traditional rabelo boat; the terraced vineyards are UNESCO-listed.

stops.name: Veladouro, Pinhão
stops.tips: A riverside tavern for lunch; try posta (veal steak) and Douro wine.

stops.name: Casal de Loivos Viewpoint
stops.tips: The best view of the valley (10 minutes by taxi); the return train is at 17:20.

backups.name: Quinta das Carvalhas
backups.tips: A vineyard on the opposite bank; jeep tour.

backups.name: Museu do Douro, Peso da Régua
backups.tips: On the way back, get off at Régua for the museum; take a later train.

stops.name: Tram 1 Ribeira–Foz
stops.tips: A 1930s wooden tram runs along the river to the Atlantic; board at the Infante stop.

stops.name: Foz do Douro Lighthouse
stops.tips: Lighthouse and crashing waves; see the Pérgola seafront columns.

stops.name: Praia dos Ingleses and Seafront
stops.tips: Foz beaches and cafés; swim in summer (the Atlantic is cold).

stops.name: Casa de Pasto da Palmeira, Foz
stops.tips: Small plates with a sea view; modern Portuguese cooking.

stops.name: Palácio de Cristal Gardens
stops.tips: Terraced gardens with peacocks; views of the river and bridge, bus 500.

backups.name: Serralves Museum
backups.tips: Siza's contemporary art museum and an Art Deco villa in a park; an alternative to the Crystal Palace.

backups.name: Brasão Cervejaria Foz
backups.tips: Francesinha (Porto's "heart attack" sandwich) with its sauce.

stops.name: Guimarães Castle
stops.tips: 1 hour by train; a 10th-century castle, the "birthplace of Portugal".

stops.name: Palace of the Dukes of Braganza
stops.tips: A Burgundian-style ducal palace; look out for the tapestries.

stops.name: Largo da Oliveira, Guimarães
stops.tips: A UNESCO medieval square; lunch at Cor de Tangerina.

stops.name: Bom Jesus do Monte, Braga
stops.tips: Take the bus or train to Braga; a Baroque zigzag staircase of 577 steps and a water-powered funicular (1882), with views.

stops.name: Braga Cathedral
stops.tips: Portugal's oldest cathedral; then the train back.

backups.name: Santuário do Sameiro
backups.tips: A sanctuary above Bom Jesus; views.

backups.name: Frigideiras do Cantinho, Braga
backups.tips: A café dating from 1796; try the frigideira pastry.

stops.name: Aveiro Moliceiro Boat
stops.tips: 1 hour by train; canal boats in the "Venice of Portugal" (45 minutes), plus Art Nouveau houses.

stops.name: Confeitaria Peixinho
stops.tips: A pastry shop from 1856; try ovos moles (egg-yolk sweets in shell shapes).

stops.name: Costa Nova Striped Houses
stops.tips: 30 minutes by bus; candy-striped fishermen's houses (palheiros) and a beach.

stops.name: Dóri, Costa Nova
stops.tips: A lagoon-side fish restaurant for lunch; try the caldeirada (fish stew).

stops.name: Praia da Costa Nova
stops.tips: Atlantic beach and dunes; then head back.

backups.name: Vista Alegre Factory
backups.tips: A porcelain factory museum; in Ílhavo.

backups.name: Salpoente Aveiro
backups.tips: A bacalhau (salt cod) tasting menu in a salt warehouse.

stops.name: Rua de Miguel Bombarda Galleries
stops.tips: A street of art galleries; Centro Comercial Bombarda for design.

stops.name: Cedofeita Neighbourhood
stops.tips: Street art (Hazul) and cafés.

stops.name: Manteigaria Porto
stops.tips: Warm pastel de nata (custard tart); near Clérigos.

stops.name: Rua das Flores
stops.tips: A pedestrian street; say goodbye with Casa Portuguesa do Pastel de Bacalhau.

stops.name: Trindade Metro to the Airport
stops.tips: Metro line E, 30 minutes; farewell.

backups.name: Bonjardim Grill
backups.tips: A street-side restaurant serving piri piri chicken.

backups.name: Casa da Música
backups.tips: Koolhaas's white concrete concert hall; tour at 11:00, an alternative to the galleries.
